change: Agent repeatability with fixed seeds and candidate-specific PCA metric evaluation
reason_for_change: Smoke-test the adaptive agent workflow while keeping the configured LLM seed, Leiden seed, initial parameters, dataset, and preprocessing fixed. Evaluation metrics use the first n_pcs PCs specified by each candidate and log metric_n_pcs.

decision.reason: Intrinsic evidence: Silhouette is low (0.116) and Davies-Bouldin is high (2.11), indicating weak separation/cohesion at the current settings. Structural evidence: 9 clusters with two very small groups (33 and 13 cells) and two T-cell–like clusters (0 and 1) showing similar markers suggest possible over-fragmentation. Lowering resolution should test whether merging closely related partitions improves separation/cohesion without enforcing a specific cluster count. Biological evidence (supporting only): Overlap of IL7R/CD27/SELL between clusters 0 and 1, and shared cytotoxic markers between clusters 2 and 6, is compatible with consolidation at slightly lower resolution, but does not determine the decision. This single-parameter change directly probes whether reduced granularity improves intrinsic metrics while maintaining reasonable structure.

Intrinsic evidence: lowering resolution from 1.0 to 0.8 modestly improved silhouette (0.116→0.122), reduced DB (2.11→2.07), and lowered within-cluster dispersion, but overall separation remains modest. Structural evidence: both settings produced 9 clusters with two persistent small clusters (33 and 13 cells) and no dominant cluster; this suggests stable fine structure but leaves uncertainty whether local connectivity is optimally captured. Biological evidence (supporting only): marker patterns across clusters are broadly compatible with diverse PBMC-related signals (e.g., antigen-presentation, cytotoxic, myeloid, platelet-like), indicating meaningful heterogeneity to preserve without forcing targets. To address the main uncertainty—whether graph construction with very small neighborhoods limits cohesion—test a moderate increase in n_neighbors to 20 while keeping the better-performing resolution and PCs fixed, which may improve separation/cohesion without arbitrarily changing granularity.

Intrinsic evidence: Increasing n_neighbors from 15 to 20 at the same resolution (0.8) reduced DBI (2.07 -> 2.02) with essentially unchanged silhouette (~0.122), while WC-dispersion changed minimally (slight increase). This suggests that modestly larger neighborhood graphs may further improve separation without clear intrinsic downside. Structural evidence: All tested settings yield 9 clusters with similar size distribution and only two very small clusters, indicating no over-fragmentation at resolution 0.8; keeping resolution fixed isolates the neighborhood-size effect. Biological evidence: Marker patterns are broadly compatible with plausible PBMC structure (e.g., IL7R+, HLA-II+, LYZ+, cytotoxic signatures, platelet-like), supporting that the observed structure is not obviously spurious, but not driving the decision.

Intrinsic evidence: At n_neighbors=30, resolution=0.8, n_pcs=30 we have the best silhouette (0.1228) and the best Davies–Bouldin (2.0229) so far, with WC-dispersion close to the best. Increasing n_neighbors from 15→20→30 has yielded small but consistent gains in separation/cohesion, suggesting further improvement may be possible. Structural evidence: Cluster number has remained stable at 9 with a reasonable size distribution; two small clusters persist but not excessively fragmented. Adjusting n_neighbors further can refine the graph without changing granularity via resolution. Biological evidence (supporting only): Marker patterns are broadly compatible with plausible PBMC structure across runs and do not argue against this configuration. To test whether the observed trend with n_neighbors continues, propose increasing n_neighbors to 40 while keeping resolution and PCs fixed to isolate its effect.

Intrinsic: At resolution 0.8, varying n_neighbors (15–40) yields very similar metrics (silhouette ~0.122, DBI slightly improving with higher neighbors, minimal WC-dispersion differences). No clear gain from further neighbor tuning; slight trade-off between best silhouette (n_neighbors=30) and best DBI (n_neighbors=40). Structural: Stable 9-cluster solutions with two small clusters and no dominant cluster inflation suggest reasonable granularity without over-fragmentation. Biological: Marker patterns are broadly compatible with plausible PBMC structure (e.g., T, B, myeloid/NK, platelet-like), supporting that clusters are not obviously spurious, but not used as targets. Next uncertainty is embedding dimensionality; testing n_pcs=40 (holding resolution and neighbors fixed) may capture additional variance and improve separation without forcing extra granularity.

Intrinsic evidence: Using 40 PCs improved separation (silhouette 0.194, DBI 1.76) relative to prior 30-PC runs (~0.12, ~2.02), but WC-dispersion increased markedly (~321k vs ~228k), suggesting merged structure. Structural evidence: Fewer clusters (7) with a dominant cluster (~45%) indicates possible under-clustering. Biological context (marker patterns broadly compatible with major PBMC compartments) suggests the large IL7R/LTB-enriched cluster may contain substructure; this is supportive but not determinative. A modest resolution increase to 0.9, holding neighbors and PCs fixed, directly tests whether reducing under-clustering can lower within-cluster dispersion and large-cluster dominance while preserving acceptable separation metrics.

Intrinsic evidence: With n_pcs=40 and resolution=0.8, metrics were strongest (silhouette 0.194, DBI 1.76). Increasing resolution to 0.9 markedly degraded separation (silhouette 0.086, DBI 2.33) despite the expected WC decrease, suggesting over-fragmentation at 0.9. Testing an intermediate resolution (0.85) may retain much of the improved intrinsic evidence while modestly increasing granularity. Structural evidence: At 0.8 there are 7 clusters with one dominant (~45%) and two very small clusters; at 0.9 there are 8 clusters with reduced dominance but more fragmentation. A slight resolution increase may split the dominant cluster without proliferating small clusters. Biological evidence: Marker patterns across runs are broadly compatible with PBMC compartments and do not contradict either granularity; they support that small clusters may be plausible but are not the basis for the decision.

Intrinsic evidence: With 40 PCs at resolution 0.8 and n_neighbors=30, silhouette (0.194) and DB (1.76) were best; increasing resolution to 0.85–0.9 sharply degraded both (silhouette ~0.086, DB >2.3), so added granularity via resolution is not supported. Structural evidence: the strong dominance of one cluster at 0.8 suggests possible under-clustering, but resolution-driven splits did not yield well-separated groups. To probe finer local structure without the metric collapse seen at higher resolution, reduce n_neighbors to 20 while keeping 40 PCs and resolution 0.8. Biological evidence: marker patterns are broadly compatible with major PBMC compartments and hint at heterogeneity within the large IL7R/LTB-enriched group, but this is only supportive context and not driving the decision.

Intrinsic: The best evidence so far is at n_neighbors=30, resolution=0.8, n_pcs=40 (highest silhouette ~0.19 and lowest DB ~1.76). The current nn=20 at the same PCs/res worsened both (silhouette ~0.17, DB ~1.93). Increasing resolution (0.85–0.9) degraded metrics, so keep resolution at 0.8. Testing higher n_neighbors (40) at 40 PCs may improve cohesion/separation via additional smoothing, as suggested by the small DB gains seen at 30 PCs when moving from 30→40 neighbors. Structural: Cluster counts and small clusters (∼26 and 13 cells) have been stable across settings, with no clear over-fragmentation. Evaluating nn=40 will test whether modest smoothing can reduce boundary noise without collapsing meaningful structure. Biological: Marker patterns are broadly compatible with major PBMC compartments across settings but are not driving the choice.

Intrinsic evidence: The best metrics so far occur near resolution 0.8 with n_pcs=40 and n_neighbors=30 (silhouette ~0.194, DBI ~1.76). Increasing resolution above 0.8 degraded silhouette and DBI, and moving n_neighbors from 30 to 40 slightly worsened both. Since moving from 30 to 40 PCs improved intrinsic metrics, testing a modest increase to 45 PCs at the same n_neighbors and resolution may yield further gains or confirm a plateau. Structural evidence: The solution at res=0.8 yields 7 clusters with a large T-cell–like cluster and two very small clusters; structure appears stable across nearby settings. We aim to refine separation without forcing extra fragmentation. Biological evidence: Marker patterns are broadly compatible with diverse PBMC compartments, supporting plausibility but not driving the decision. Testing n_pcs=45 focuses on intrinsic separation while keeping structure similar.

Intrinsic evidence: With n_pcs=40 at resolution 0.8, metrics were strongest so far (highest silhouette ~0.194, lowest DB ~1.76). Increasing resolution to 0.85–0.9 degraded silhouette and DB markedly, and raising n_pcs to 45 also worsened both and increased WC-dispersion. This suggests the sweet spot is around 40 PCs and mid resolution; a key uncertainty is whether slightly lower resolution could further improve separation. Structural evidence: Two very small clusters persist across settings and one dominant large cluster remains, indicating marginal splits among closely related cells; modestly lowering resolution may merge weak boundaries without over-fragmentation. Biological evidence (supporting only): Marker patterns are broadly compatible with major PBMC compartments, but do not mandate additional splitting. Testing a small decrease in resolution (to 0.7) while holding the otherwise best-performing settings constant targets the main uncertainty with a single, informative change.

Intrinsic: The best separation so far is at n_neighbors≈30–40, resolution 0.7–0.8 with n_pcs=40 (silhouette ~0.19, DBI ~1.76–1.77). n_pcs=45 degraded metrics and n_pcs=30 was much worse. WC-dispersion increased at 40 PCs versus 30, suggesting some added noise; testing 35 PCs may preserve the improved silhouette/DBI while reducing within-cluster dispersion. Structural: This regime yields 7 clusters with two very small clusters and a ~45% dominant cluster; increasing resolution above 0.8 fragmented structure and worsened intrinsic metrics, so further splitting is not supported. Adjusting PCs is a targeted, lower-risk refinement. Biological: Marker patterns are broadly compatible with plausible PBMC compartments, supporting that the structure is reasonable, but they are not used to drive the choice.

Intrinsic evidence: The current configuration yields the best overall separation to date (silhouette 0.209, highest so far; Davies–Bouldin 1.659, lowest so far). Although WC-dispersion is higher than at 30 PCs, prior runs show that increasing PCs tends to inflate dispersion; the simultaneous improvement in silhouette and DB indicates a net gain in cluster quality. Structural evidence: 7 clusters with limited fragmentation and only two very small clusters (27, 13), a pattern that has been stable across settings. A large cluster (~44%) persists across configurations; prior adjustments (higher resolution or different n_neighbors at similar PCs) did not improve intrinsic metrics and often degraded them, suggesting limited upside from further tuning. Biological evidence (context only): Marker patterns are broadly compatible with major PBMC compartments and rare populations, providing supportive context without dictating the choice. Given the strong intrinsic metrics and stable structure, further exploration is unlikely to yield meaningful gains.

final_result.final_selection_reason: 1) Strongest intrinsic evidence: iteration 12. It has the highest silhouette (0.209) and the lowest Davies–Bouldin (1.659) among all runs; WC-dispersion is reasonable, noting WC can shift with n_pcs, and overall intrinsic improvement over the 30-PC/9-cluster solutions is substantial. 2) Most reasonable cluster structure: iteration 12. It yields 7 clusters with one large T-cell–like group (~44%) but also a separate cytotoxic-like group and two monocyte-like groups; only two very small clusters (27, 13) that recur across many runs, suggesting stability rather than over-fragmentation. Higher-resolution 9-cluster runs introduce more splits without intrinsic gains. 3) Biological evidence: supporting. Marker patterns are consistent with broad PBMC compartments (e.g., IL7R/LTB-rich T cells, NKG7/CST7 cytotoxic compartment, CD74/HLA-DRA B-like, LST1/FCGR3A monocyte subsets, HLA-DP/DR small dendritic-like, PF4 platelet-like), with no contradictions. 4) Ultimately selected: iteration 12. 5) The final selection matches the strongest intrinsic candidate; no structural or biological evidence justifies choosing a different experiment.
